question.text: SEBI-categorized Retirement Fund schemes have a minimum lock-in period of:

answer.text: 5 years or till retirement age, whichever is earlier
Till age 60, no early exit allowed

explanation.text: The Logic: Retirement Fund schemes have a lock-in of at least five years or till retirement age, whichever is earlier. Children's Fund schemes follow a parallel rule with a lock-in of five years or till the child attains majority, whichever is earlier. The Trap: The lock-in ends at whichever event arrives EARLIER — the completion of five years or reaching retirement age. It is not whichever is later. Note: Solution-oriented schemes use this lock-in structure to align with the underlying life-stage goal.
